questions.q: What are your eating habits?
questions.a: Overall, I think I {{have::simple_present}} fairly healthy and balanced eating habits. questions.q: What do you think of junk food?
questions.a: In my view, junk food {{tastes::present_simple}} very good and convenient, but it {{is::be}} very harmful to our health if we eat it frequently. questions.q: Are you concerned about your daily calorie intake when choosing something to eat?
questions.a: I {{pay::present_simple}} some attention to calories, but I am not obsessed with counting every single number. If I {{notice::present_simple}} that I am gaining a little weight, I simply {{reduce::present_simple}} my portions of bread, rice, and sweets for a few weeks.

questions.q: What foods have a lot of calories?
questions.a: There {{are::be}} many foods that contain a very high number of calories, both healthy and unhealthy ones. Unhealthy high-calorie foods usually {{include::present_simple}} fried fast food, like French fries, crispy chicken, and cheeseburgers. On the other hand, there {{are::be}} also many healthy foods that are naturally calorie-dense. For instance, nuts like walnuts and almonds, seeds, olive oil, cheese, and avocados {{have::present_simple}} a lot of calories because of their healthy fats. While healthy high-calorie foods {{are::be}} good for our bodies in small amounts, we should always watch our portion sizes so we do not gain unwanted weight.

questions.q: Do you think fast food, soda and sweets should be sold in school cafeterias?
questions.a: No, I strongly {{believe::present_simple}} that fast food, sugary sodas, and sweets should not be sold in school cafeterias. Schools {{have::simple_present}} an important responsibility to protect children's health and teach them good lifestyle habits. Children and teenagers often {{do not::present_simple}} have the discipline to make healthy food choices on their own. Instead, school cafeterias {{should offer::modal}} fresh fruits, warm vegetable soups, whole-wheat sandwiches, and natural juices. Providing nutritious options at school {{helps::present_simple}} children build healthy eating habits that last a lifetime.

questions.q: What kind of food do you think is the least/most healthy?
questions.a: In my opinion, the healthiest foods {{are::be}} whole, unprocessed foods that come directly from nature. Fresh green vegetables, seasonal fruits, legumes, nuts, fish, and whole grains {{are::be}} the best options because they provide essential vitamins, minerals, and dietary fiber that protect our organs. Fresh salmon and olive oil, for example, {{are::be}} fantastic for heart and brain health. On the other hand, the least healthy foods {{are::be}} ultra-processed foods and deep-fried items. Things like packaged hot dogs, potato chips, instant noodles, and sugary energy drinks {{are::be}} extremely bad for our bodies. They {{are::be}} full of artificial chemicals, trans fats, refined sugar, and excessive salt. Eating them regularly {{damages::present_simple}} your blood vessels and significantly increases the risk of chronic illnesses.

questions.q: How good are you at cooking?

questions.q: Who is the best cook among your family, relatives and friends?
questions.a: Without any doubt, the best cook in my entire family {{is::be}} my grandmother. questions.a: In my opinion, traditional slow-cooked stews and delicate pastries {{are::be}} the hardest things to cook properly. If you {{make::present_simple}} a small mistake with the amount of flour or yeast, or if the oven temperature {{is::be}} slightly too hot, the cake will completely ruin. questions.q: Is it important for husbands to know how to cook?
questions.a: Yes, I think it {{is::be}} extremely important for husbands to know how to cook. questions.q: Are cooking shows popular in your country? Do you watch them?
questions.a: Yes, cooking shows {{are::be}} very popular in my country, and many people watch them regularly on television and social media. questions.q: What are some of the benefits of cooking your meals at home?
questions.a: Cooking meals at home {{has::present_simple}} many fantastic benefits for your health, your wallet, and your daily life. questions.a: Yes, I definitely {{notice::present_simple}} that my emotions have a strong effect on my eating habits. questions.q: What’s the most important meal for Iranians?
questions.a: In Iranian culture, lunch {{is::be}} traditionally considered the most important and elaborate meal of the day. Families usually {{take::present_simple}} lunch very seriously, and it is often a warm, sit-down meal that everyone enjoys together. A typical Iranian lunch {{consists::present_simple}} of a large platter of aromatic Persian rice topped with saffron, served alongside a rich, slow-cooked stew known as khoresh, such as Ghormeh Sabzi. We also {{love::present_simple}} grilled kebabs with grilled tomatoes and fresh herbs on the side. Lunch {{is accompanied::present_simple}} by traditional side dishes like fresh flatbread, plain yogurt, and a crisp salad made with diced cucumbers, tomatoes, and onions. Because lunch {{is::be}} so hearty and filling, people often {{drink::present_simple}} hot black tea afterward and {{take::present_simple}} a short rest before continuing their afternoon work. While dinner is also eaten with family, it is usually much lighter, making lunch the true culinary highlight of our daily routine.

questions.q: What changes do we need to make in our daily diet?
questions.a: I {{believe::present_simple}} most of us need to make a few simple but important changes to improve our daily diet. First, we {{should cut down::modal}} on processed foods, sugary drinks, and fast food. Many people {{drink::present_simple}} soda or eat packaged chips every afternoon, which adds unnecessary calories and unhealthy fats to their bodies. Instead of drinking soda, we {{should drink::modal}} plenty of plain water, herbal teas, or fresh fruit juice. Second, we {{need to eat::modal}} more fresh fruits and green vegetables every single day. Adding a fresh green salad to lunch and dinner {{is::be}} an easy way to get essential vitamins and fiber. In addition, we {{should replace::modal}} white bread and refined grains with whole-wheat options like brown rice, oats, and whole-grain bread. Finally, reducing our salt intake and cooking with healthy oils like olive oil instead of solid fats will {{protect::modal}} our heart health and give us lasting energy throughout the day.

questions.a: Yes, I absolutely {{love::present_simple}} trying food from other countries! questions.q: Why is it important to eat your meal with your family?
questions.a: Eating meals together as a family {{is::be}} extremely important because it builds strong emotional connections and brings everyone closer. During dinner, family members can {{turn off::modal}} the television, put away their mobile phones, and talk openly about their day. Parents can {{listen::modal}} to their children's experiences, offer helpful advice, and share funny stories. This habit {{creates::present_simple}} a supportive, loving atmosphere where everyone feels heard and valued. Furthermore, research {{shows::present_simple}} that children who regularly eat dinner with their parents develop healthier eating habits, do better in school, and feel more emotionally secure. A shared meal {{nourishes::present_simple}} not only the body, but also the heart and family bond.

questions.q: Why do you think staying on a diet is difficult?
questions.a: Staying on a diet is often very difficult because it {{requires::present_simple}} strong willpower, careful planning, and major changes to daily habits. First of all, unhealthy food {{is::be}} everywhere and is very convenient. Second, social situations {{make::present_simple}} dieting challenging. When you {{go::present_simple}} out with friends or attend a family party, everyone is eating cake and rich food, so saying no feels awkward. Another major reason is that many diets {{are::be}} too strict. When people completely cut out carbohydrates or their favorite treats, they quickly {{feel::present_simple}} hungry, tired, and frustrated. Eventually, they {{give::present_simple}} up and return to their old eating patterns. To succeed, people {{need::present_simple}} a balanced, sustainable lifestyle rather than an extreme, temporary diet.

questions.q: Why do people become vegetarian?
questions.a: People {{choose::present_simple}} to become vegetarian for several different reasons, including health benefits, ethical beliefs, and environmental concerns. First, many individuals {{stop::present_simple}} eating meat because they want to protect their physical health. Studies {{show::present_simple}} that a vegetarian diet rich in vegetables, beans, nuts, and fruits can lower blood pressure, reduce cholesterol, and decrease the risk of heart disease. Second, ethical concerns {{are::be}} a powerful motivator for many people. They {{love::present_simple}} animals and do not want living creatures to suffer or be killed for food. They {{believe::present_simple}} that all animals deserve respect and kindness. Third, environmental protection {{has become::present_perfect}} a major reason in recent years. Raising livestock {{consumes::present_simple}} enormous amounts of fresh water, causes deforestation, and produces greenhouse gases. By eating plant-based foods instead of beef, vegetarians {{hope::present_simple}} to reduce their personal carbon footprint and help protect the future of our planet.

questions.q: What strategies do you use (or recommend) to reduce unhealthy habits, like cutting down on sugar?
questions.a: To cut down on sugar and build healthier eating habits, I {{recommend::present_simple}} using practical, step-by-step strategies rather than trying to change everything overnight. First, stop buying sugary snacks and sodas at the supermarket. If you {{do not::present_simple}} keep cookies, candy, and soda in your kitchen cupboards, you will not eat them when you feel bored at home. Second, replace sugary items with delicious, natural alternatives. For example, when you {{crave::present_simple}} something sweet after lunch, eat an apple, a banana, or a handful of sweet dates with plain tea instead of eating chocolate cake. Third, drink plenty of water throughout the day. Often, when people think they want sugar, their body {{is::be}} simply thirsty. Another great tip is to read food labels carefully when grocery shopping, because hidden sugars {{are added::present_simple}} to sauces, breads, and canned goods. Making small, gradual adjustments {{makes::present_simple}} it much easier to maintain a healthy lifestyle long-term.

questions.q: Do you think society prioritizes 'balanced meals' enough? What barriers prevent people from eating this way consistently?
questions.a: No, I {{do not::present_simple}} think our society prioritizes balanced meals enough today. While people {{talk::present_simple}} a lot about health and wellness online, modern life {{makes::present_simple}} it very hard for average citizens to eat balanced meals consistently. The biggest barrier {{is::be}} a lack of time. Most people {{work::present_simple}} long hours and commute in heavy traffic, so when they get home exhausted, they do not have the time or energy to cook balanced meals from scratch. Another major barrier {{is::be}} financial cost. In many cities, fresh organic vegetables and high-quality lean meats {{are::be}} much more expensive than cheap, processed junk food. Furthermore, aggressive advertising constantly {{promotes::present_simple}} sugary snacks and greasy fast food to children on TV and social media. Fast-food restaurants {{are::be}} on every corner, making unhealthy choices too convenient. Until healthy food {{becomes::present_simple}} affordable and quick, people will continue to struggle.

questions.q: How do you manage cravings, like a 'sweet tooth'? Are cravings more psychological or biological, in your opinion?
questions.a: In my opinion, cravings {{are::be}} a combination of biological signals and psychological habits, but psychology often {{plays::present_simple}} a bigger role. Biologically, when our blood sugar {{drops::present_simple}} or when we {{are::be}} very tired, our body naturally asks for quick energy in the form of sugar and simple carbohydrates. However, psychologically, we frequently {{use::present_simple}} sweet treats as an emotional reward or a way to cope with boredom, stress, and sadness. To manage my own sweet tooth, I {{use::present_simple}} a few reliable methods. First, I {{drink::present_simple}} a large glass of water or a cup of warm cinnamon tea, which usually makes the craving disappear. Second, if I still {{want::present_simple}} something sweet, I eat fresh fruit or a small piece of dark chocolate instead of a heavy pastry. I also {{distract::present_simple}} myself by going for a short walk or calling a friend, which breaks the mental habit of emotional snacking.

questions.q: What causes someone to become a picky eater? Were you picky?
questions.a: Several factors {{cause::present_simple}} someone to become a picky eater, including childhood experiences, genetics, and texture sensitivities. Some people {{are born::present_simple}} with sensitive taste buds, so strong flavors like bitter greens or spicy peppers taste overwhelming to them. In other cases, children {{become::present_simple}} picky because their parents never introduced diverse foods when they were young, or because parents forced them to eat things they disliked, creating negative memories around mealtime. As a child, I {{was::simple_past}} definitely a picky eater. I {{refused::simple_past}} to eat cooked vegetables, especially onions, eggplants, and mushrooms, because I {{hated::simple_past}} their soft texture. Whenever my mother {{cooked::simple_past}} stews with eggplants, I carefully {{picked::simple_past}} them out of my plate and left them behind. However, as I {{grew::simple_past}} older, my palate matured, and I began trying new cooking styles. Today, I {{eat::present_simple}} almost everything, and I actually {{love::present_simple}} the very foods that I used to dislike when I was small.

questions.q: Are 'cheat days' helpful for maintaining a healthy diet, or do they encourage unhealthy cycles? Share your perspective.
questions.a: I think cheat days can be helpful if they are used sensibly, but they can easily encourage unhealthy cycles if people lose control. On the positive side, having a planned cheat meal gives you something enjoyable to look forward to during a week of strict eating. It {{provides::present_simple}} psychological relief, reduces feelings of deprivation, and helps you stay motivated when you are following a healthy nutrition plan. However, dedicating an entire day to uncontrolled eating can be dangerous. Some people {{eat::present_simple}} huge quantities of greasy burgers, chips, and ice cream all day long, which can ruin their weekly progress and cause digestive discomfort and feelings of guilt. Therefore, instead of a full 'cheat day,' I strongly {{recommend::present_simple}} having a single 'cheat meal' once a week. This {{allows::present_simple}} you to enjoy your favorite pizza or dessert with friends without creating an unhealthy cycle of starving and overeating.

questions.q: Have you experienced being 'hangry'? How can people manage their mood when hungry, and why does hunger affect emotions so strongly?
questions.a: Yes, I have definitely {{experienced::present_perfect}} being 'hangry' many times! When I {{skip::present_simple}} a meal and get very hungry, I become irritable, impatient, and easily annoyed by little things. This {{happens::present_simple}} because hunger affects our biology directly. When we do not eat for many hours, our blood glucose levels {{drop::present_simple}} significantly. Since the brain relies on glucose for energy, a drop in blood sugar {{triggers::present_simple}} stress hormones like adrenaline and cortisol, which makes us feel anxious, short-tempered, and aggressive. To manage this mood, people {{should keep::modal}} healthy snacks with them wherever they go. Carrying a small bag of almonds, walnuts, or a banana in your bag can save you from a bad mood when you are stuck in traffic or working late. In addition, when you {{notice::present_simple}} that you are feeling angry for no reason, pause, recognize your hunger, drink water, and eat a balanced snack before having difficult conversations.

questions.q: Do you feel guilty about eating unhealthy foods?
questions.a: Yes, to be completely honest, I sometimes {{feel::present_simple}} guilty after eating unhealthy foods, especially when I eat them late at night. For example, if I {{eat::present_simple}} a large bag of potato chips while watching television or finish a big slice of chocolate cake after dinner, I often {{regret::present_simple}} it immediately afterward. I {{feel::present_simple}} bad because I know that processed foods are harmful to my physical health and skin, and they make me feel heavy and sluggish the next morning. However, I {{am learning::present_continuous}} not to be too hard on myself. Feeling guilty about food can {{create::modal}} a negative relationship with eating, which is unhealthy for the mind. Now, instead of feeling guilty, I {{try::present_simple}} to practice moderation. If I enjoy a delicious dessert or fast food with my friends on Friday, I simply {{accept::present_simple}} it as a treat and return to eating fresh vegetables and home-cooked meals the next day.

questions.q: Is eating to cope with emotions (like sadness) harmful, or a valid way to self-soothe? What alternatives exist for processing emotions?
questions.a: Eating to cope with difficult emotions is understandable, but it is ultimately harmful if it becomes a regular habit. While eating warm comfort foods like cookies or pasta {{provides::present_simple}} temporary relief, it does not solve the underlying emotional problem. Once the temporary pleasure of the food {{disappears::present_simple}}, the original sadness or stress remains, often accompanied by regret and physical discomfort. Over time, emotional eating can {{lead::modal}} to weight gain, low energy, and poor health. Fortunately, there are many healthier alternatives for processing negative emotions. When you {{feel::present_simple}} sad or overwhelmed, going for a thirty-minute walk in a quiet park can {{clear::modal}} your head and boost your mood. Talking to a close friend or family member {{provides::present_simple}} genuine emotional support and makes you feel heard. Other wonderful activities include writing your feelings in a personal journal, taking a warm bath, listening to soothing music, or doing light stretching exercises.

questions.q: What food would you miss the most if you became vegetarian?
questions.a: If I ever {{decided::simple_past}} to become a vegetarian, the food I would miss the most would definitely be traditional Persian grilled kebabs, particularly Kabab Koobideh. Kabab Koobideh {{is::be}} seasoned minced meat grilled over hot charcoal skewers, and it has an incredible smoky flavor and tender texture. In our culture, eating kebabs with saffron rice, grilled tomatoes, and sumac {{is::be}} a special tradition during family gatherings, holidays, and celebrations. No plant-based substitute can truly {{match::modal}} the rich taste and nostalgic feeling of freshly grilled kebabs. In addition to kebabs, I would also {{miss::modal}} roasted chicken and slow-cooked meat stews like Ghormeh Sabzi, where tender pieces of beef absorb all the rich herbs and dried limes. While I {{enjoy::present_simple}} fresh vegetables and grains, living without traditional meat dishes would be a huge challenge for me, so I {{prefer::present_simple}} eating meat in moderation rather than giving it up completely.

questions.q: How can individuals and societies reduce food waste while ensuring food safety?
questions.a: Both individuals and societies can {{take::modal}} practical, effective steps to reduce food waste while keeping food safe to eat. At the individual level, people {{should plan::modal}} their meals before going to the supermarket and write a clear shopping list. This {{prevents::present_simple}} impulse buying and stops fresh vegetables from rotting in the refrigerator. In addition, people {{should learn::modal}} how to store food properly. Putting leftovers into airtight glass containers and freezing extra portions {{keeps::present_simple}} meals safe and fresh for days. At the societal level, supermarkets and bakeries {{should donate::modal}} unsold, safe food to local food banks and charity organizations instead of throwing it into the trash at the end of the day. Restaurants {{can offer::modal}} different portion sizes so customers do not leave large amounts of food uneaten on their plates. Finally, public campaigns {{can teach::modal}} people the difference between 'use-by' dates for safety and 'best-before' dates for quality.

questions.q: How many meals a day do you think should be eaten?
questions.a: How many meals a person should eat each day really {{depends::present_simple}} on their daily schedule, energy needs, and lifestyle, but I think eating three balanced meals is ideal for most people. A good breakfast in the morning {{kickstarts::present_simple}} your metabolism and gives you the energy you need to focus on work or study. A nutritious lunch in the middle of the day {{restores::present_simple}} your strength and keeps you productive throughout the afternoon. Finally, a moderate, lighter dinner in the evening {{satisfies::present_simple}} your hunger without disturbing your sleep at night. In addition to these three main meals, having one or two small, healthy snacks—such as a piece of fresh fruit or a handful of raw nuts—can {{prevent::modal}} extreme hunger and overeating. The most important thing is not counting exact meals, but listening to your body's hunger cues, maintaining steady energy, and avoiding heavy meals right before bedtime.

questions.q: Is it important to have a fixed eating time?
questions.a: Yes, I {{believe::present_simple}} that having a fixed eating time is very important for maintaining good physical health and digestive wellness. When you {{eat::present_simple}} your meals at the same hours every day, your body {{develops::present_simple}} a natural biological rhythm. Your digestive system {{knows::present_simple}} when to expect food, so it {{produces::present_simple}} digestive enzymes efficiently, preventing problems like indigestion, acid reflux, and bloating. In addition, regular meal times {{help::present_simple}} regulate your blood sugar and energy levels, which prevents sudden energy crashes, afternoon fatigue, and intense cravings for sugary snacks. However, having a routine does not mean you must be overly strict. If work or travel delays your meal by an hour, that is perfectly fine. The goal is to maintain general consistency so that you do not skip meals or eat heavy dinners very late at night, both of which can disrupt your sleep and overall health.

questions.q: What are super foods?
questions.a: 'Superfoods' is a term used to describe nutrient-dense foods that contain an exceptionally high concentration of vitamins, minerals, antioxidants, and healthy fats. These foods {{offer::present_simple}} significant health benefits and help protect the human body from chronic diseases, inflammation, and fatigue. Some famous examples of superfoods include blueberries, which {{are::be}} loaded with antioxidants that protect our cells, and avocados, which {{provide::present_simple}} heart-healthy unsaturated fats. Other popular superfoods {{are::be}} green leafy vegetables like spinach and kale, nuts such as walnuts and almonds, and seeds like chia seeds and flaxseeds. Fatty fish like salmon, rich in omega-3 fatty acids, is also considered a superfood. While eating these nutritious foods {{is::be}} certainly beneficial for boosting energy and immunity, it is important to remember that no single food can perform miracles on its own. The best approach is eating a wide variety of colorful, whole foods as part of a balanced daily diet.
